comment: Mode S replies and ADS-B extended squitters at 1090 MHz: pulse position modulation at 1 Mb/s, a bit a pulse in the first (1) or the second (0) half of its microsecond, after a preamble of four pulses. The capture is the channel at 2 MS/s, one sample per half-microsecond chip: the envelope, scaled by the pulses' peak (so each burst sets its own level), is sliced into on/off chips; the preamble delimits a frame (matched exactly: with an error allowed, the tail of a frame passes for one), the chip pairs decode as Manchester (Thomas sense; a pair of two equal chips is no bit and fails its frame, so silence never passes the parity), the downlink format gives the length and the 24-bit parity accepts the frame. Out come the bits between DF and parity of every clean reply. Transmitting: `fields={"df": 17}` per frame (default 17), the preamble chips before each
